scope: STATIC TRACE of the id read: the arguments say bits 1309..1320 = 8, yet the stored word measured 4048 - so the store instruction must be sampled directly

the_static_trace.0x67168F: call 0x66ED70 - the byte-based count reader; it advances [+0x1C] only, not [+0x20]
the_static_trace.0x671698: mov [0x7859558], al - the count byte is stored
the_static_trace.0x67169D: test al,al ; je 0x6716C3 - skip the loop when the count is 0
the_static_trace.0x6716A3: mov eax,esi - eax = the stream (esi is the function's stream argument)
the_static_trace.0x6716A5: call 0x66EC30 - reads 12 bits from [+0x20] of that stream
the_static_trace.0x6716AD: mov word [ecx*2 + 0x7859358], ax - store the returned value

the_reasoning_that_should_hold: 0x66ED70 advances only [+0x1C], so [+0x20] is unchanged by the count read
the two gate bits at 1307 and 1308 advanced [+0x20] to 1309
so the 12-bit read starts at bit 1309
bits 1309..1320 of the body are 000100000000, which is 8
0x66EC30 masks to N bits and returns that value, so ax should be 8
and the store writes it to word[0] of 0x7859358
the_contradiction: so at least one of the steps above is wrong, and the candidates are: [+0x20] is not 1309 at that moment, the body bits are not what the file says, or the store is not the one I identified
the_direct_way_to_settle_it: probe 0x6716AD (the store instruction, once per entity, not on a hot path) and log eax, bl, and [+0x20] of the stream via esi
that binds the returned value, the loop index and the read position in one record, and it cannot corrupt the parse the way a per-bit probe does
